items.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem
items.body:
llama.cpp makes it possible to run multi-modal LLMs across a wide range of hardware - from consumer-grade local machines to high-end enterprise servers. Through quantization, optimized backends, and a portable C/C++ implementation, we make AI inference accessible at every level of the software stack. We believe this is the most lightweight, versatile and sensible platform for building cross-platform and private AI products.

During the 3.5 years since its inception, the project has grown a lot and many downstream applications already depend on our work. We expect this trend to continue as local AI and privacy become increasingly important in our everyday lives. Every new integration means more developers depending on our library interfaces and therefore having a flexible but stable API is paramount.

Today we release libraries v1.0.0, highlighting our responsibility to those developers. Moving forward, both llama.cpp and ggml will reflect API and ABI incompatibilities with major-version bumps. As adoption grows, we will be stricter about making those boundaries visible to downstream consumers.

The following rules apply to all ggml-org projects using semantic versioning:

We are looking forward to expanding the ways in which ggml-org software is distributed and reaches developers and end-users. For more information about how to add ggml-org projects to your packaging and release pipelines, please check the following discussion.

The project has fostered an amazing open-source community with highly-skilled and talented contributors. With the rapid advance of AI capabilities in the field of software engineering, we continue to adapt and integrate LLMs in our developement cycle in a thoughtful and resonable manner. Maintaining a high quality codebase, staying in control of the architecture and understanding the implementation details will remain our top priorities.

To reinforce the faster pace of development we continue to invest more and more resources in improving the CI infrastructure behind the projects. Thanks to HF technologies such as HF Buckets and HF Jobs we are able to scale the capacity necessary to guarantee correctness for every change that lands on the master branches. With hardware support from NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM and Intel, we continue to enroll more self-hosted runners across all major hardware platforms.

The underlying machine learning engine of llama.cpp - ggml is designed to run on virtually any hardware in existence. This is achieved by implementing dedicated ggml backends. Each backend can be compiled as a dynamic library and optionally loaded at runtime.

A complete list of the currently implemented backends can be found here.

We are committed to provide continuous support of all model architectures. Currently, llama.cpp supports more than 150 architecture variants as well as all mainstream speculative decoding methods.

The llama.cpp team at Hugging Face is thankful for the incredible support from the community. Special thanks to the long-time maintainers of the project and all contributors. This is a significant milestone which would not have been possible without our joint efforts!

Check out Llama desktop apps for MacOS and Windows, shipped with love by the team behind llama.cpp and Hugging Face.

items.body_ko:
llama.cpp는 소비자용 로컬 기기부터 고성능 엔터프라이즈 서버에 이르는 광범위한 하드웨어에서 멀티모달 LLM을 실행할 수 있게 해줍니다. 퀀타이제이션, 최적화된 백엔드 및 이식성 좋은 C/C++ 구현을 통해 AI 추론을 소프트웨어 스택의 모든 수준에서 접근 가능하게 만듭니다. 우리는 이것이 크로스 플랫폼 및 프라이빗 AI 제품을 구축하기 위한 가장 가볍고 다재다능하며 합리적인 플랫폼이라고 믿습니다.

시작된 지 3.5년 동안 이 프로젝트는 크게 성장했으며, 이미 많은 다운스트림 애플리케이션이 우리의 작업에 의존하고 있습니다. 로컬 AI와 프라이버시가 우리 일상생활에서 점점 더 중요해짐에 따라 이러한 추세는 계속될 것으로 예상합니다. 새로운 통합은 더 많은 개발자가 우리의 라이브러리 인터페이스에 의존한다는 것을 의미하며, 따라서 유연하면서도 안정적인 API를 갖는 것이 가장 중요합니다.

오늘 우리는 개발자들에 대한 우리의 책임을 강조하며 라이브러리 v1.0.0을 출시합니다. 앞으로 llama.cpp와 ggml 모두 주요 버전 업그레이드를 통해 API 및 ABI 비호환성을 반영할 것입니다. 채택이 증가함에 따라 우리는 다운스트림 소비자에게 이러한 경계를 더욱 엄격하게 알릴 것입니다.

시맨틱 버저닝을 사용하는 모든 ggml-org 프로젝트에는 다음 규칙이 적용됩니다.

ggml-org 소프트웨어가 배포되고 개발자와 최종 사용자에게 도달하는 방식을 확장하기를 기대합니다. ggml-org 프로젝트를 패키징 및 릴리스 파이프라인에 추가하는 방법에 대한 자세한 내용은 다음 토론을 확인하십시오.

이 프로젝트는 매우 숙련되고 재능 있는 기여자들과 함께 놀라운 오픈 소스 커뮤니티를 육성했습니다. 소프트웨어 공학 분야에서 AI 기능의 급속한 발전에 발맞춰 우리는 개발 주기에서 LLM을 사려 깊고 합리적인 방식으로 계속 적응하고 통합합니다. 고품질 코드베이스를 유지하고, 아키텍처를 제어하며, 구현 세부 사항을 이해하는 것이 우리의 최우선 과제로 남을 것입니다.

더 빠른 개발 속도를 강화하기 위해 우리는 프로젝트 뒤에 있는 CI 인프라를 개선하는 데 점점 더 많은 자원을 투자하고 있습니다. HF Buckets 및 HF Jobs와 같은 HF 기술 덕분에 마스터 브랜치에 착륙하는 모든 변경 사항에 대한 정확성을 보장하는 데 필요한 용량을 확장할 수 있습니다. NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM 및 Intel의 하드웨어 지원을 통해 우리는 모든 주요 하드웨어 플랫폼에서 더 많은 자체 호스팅 러너를 계속 등록하고 있습니다.

llama.cpp의 기본 머신러닝 엔진인 ggml은 사실상 현존하는 모든 하드웨어에서 실행되도록 설계되었습니다. 이는 전용 ggml 백엔드를 구현함으로써 달성됩니다. 각 백엔드는 동적 라이브러리로 컴파일될 수 있으며 런타임에 선택적으로 로드될 수 있습니다.

현재 구현된 백엔드의 전체 목록은 여기에서 찾을 수 있습니다.

우리는 모든 모델 아키텍처에 대한 지속적인 지원을 제공하기 위해 최선을 다하고 있습니다. 현재 llama.cpp는 150개 이상의 아키텍처 변형과 모든 주류 추론 디코딩 방법을 지원합니다.

Hugging Face의 llama.cpp 팀은 커뮤니티의 놀라운 지원에 감사드립니다. 프로젝트의 오랜 관리자들과 모든 기여자들에게 특별한 감사를 전합니다. 이것은 우리의 공동 노력 없이는 불가능했을 중요한 이정표입니다!

items.title: AI unlocks Gödel's notebooks, said to contain hundreds of proved theorems
items.body:
Kurt Gödel left 1,009 pages of densely written text – much of it in an obsolete shorthand – which is now said to contain hundreds of proved theorems

The Austrian logician Kurt Gödel was one of the most original thinkers of the 20th century. His two incompleteness theorems, published in 1931, transformed mathematics and paved the way for the digital age.

After his seminal results of the 1930s, Gödel published only a few papers. His unpublished work, however, runs to tens of thousands of pages, and is of great interest to historians of science.

Since 2017, the Finnish logician Jan von Plato has led a project at Helsinki University to understand the contents of 16 notebooks that Gödel wrote in the early 1940s. This material – the “workbooks” – is 1,009 pages of densely written text about maths and logic. Much of it is written in a German shorthand, Gabelsberger, that was obsolete even when Gödel was using it.

Progress in the mathematical understanding of the text was painfully slow – about a page a week – until September, when von Plato enlisted the help of the AI model Claude. Within a couple of days, Claude had provided a comprehensive digest of the entire material, revealing Gödel had proved hundreds of theorems that no one knew about.

The most famous logician of modern times had, in fact, discovered significantly more than anyone had thought.

“I was flabbergasted,” said von Plato. “The workbooks not only contain dozens of anticipations of results not known until the 70s and 80s, but they also contain 14 themes in logic that have not been pursued. Gödel was far ahead of his time.”

Gödel changed the course of logic because he revealed the limits of mathematical knowledge. His incompleteness theorems show that in all mathematical systems there are true statements that can neither be proved or disproved. Yet while this result was a blow to previous generations of logicians, who had hoped that all truths were verifiable, Gödel’s work pushed the field in new directions, inspiring Alan Turing to write his 1936 paper that began the theory of modern computation.

In 1940, Gödel fled Austria under the Nazis. He settled in Princeton, New Jersey, and became a close friend of Albert Einstein at the Institute of Advanced Study. Increasingly paranoid in his later years, he refused to eat food that was not cooked by his wife, and died of starvation in 1978.

Von Plato said he had started his Gödel project in 2017 because he was facing mandatory retirement from Helsinki University. “What should I do to make myself indispensable? Oh yes, I’ll start reading Gödel’s enigmatic shorthand pages!” He received a €2.5m (£2.1m) grant from the European Research Council, taught himself Gabelsberger shorthand – “I am one of only six people who can read it in the world” – and assembled a small team.

In August, at a conference in France about AI and theorem proving, von Plato met computer scientists who suggested that he co-opt the help of Claude in trying to make sense of the workbooks. On his return to Helsinki he began the process, showing Claude his transcriptions of the workbooks, as well as six books he had previously written on Gödel and other secondary scientific literature.

“In a couple of days, I got to see a 650-page explanation of the workbooks. It had to be controlled page for page, but it’s basically a work that is impossible to do for human beings,” he said. “Humans read one page at a time and we tend to forget things. It takes us a year to read about 50 pages. We just are not able to keep in mind all the different parts.

“The AI can connect all the pieces in a thousand pages. It can see all of Gödel’s writings as one piece.”

Gödel’s incompleteness theorems revealed the existence of statements whose truths were independent of the system they were written in: that is, they could not be proved or disproved within the system. In 1966, the American mathematician Paul Cohen won the Fields medal, the highest honour in maths, for showing the independence of two well-known mathematical statements: the continuum hypothesis and the axiom of choice.

Gödel reacted to Cohen’s Fields medal by saying that he had already proved the result in the 1940s. Yet when pushed for a proof by his peers, Gödel was unable to reconstruct one from his notes.

The first task von Plato set Claude was to discover if Gödel’s workbooks had a proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, which would reveal that Gödel had been telling the truth in 1966. The answer came back: yes, almost. “He was just one step away,” said von Plato. “There’s one definition that Gödel got wrong, but he had the right definition two years earlier, and so the thought is that he would have arrived at the right definition anyway if he had just continued for a few months. For me, the architecture of his proof is just wonderful. It makes all of these results of set theory follow a uniform pattern.

“What strikes me especially is that he starts from ideas. He’s not like someone who plays with formulas and hopes to arrive somewhere. He has very, very clear ideas, and then he’s methodical. Step after step he goes ahead and he manages to fulfil the aims that he has in this formal work.”

Von Plato said that when Claude presented him with the reconstructed proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, he ran it through the proof assistant Coq, a program that verifies the validity of mathematical proofs, and it passed. Von Plato believes that had Gödel published his work on the axiom of choice, he would have won the 1940 Fields medal. “Maybe he felt that when Cohen got the medal, that that was something he sort of missed.”

In further discussions with Claude, von Plato asked the AI model to extract all theorems in the workbooks for which Gödel either had a proof, had sketched a proof or had an idea for a proof. Claude found 663. When these results were put into Coq: “About 400 were verified as stated, about 200 were repaired, meaning that perhaps the statement of the theorem had to be made more precise, or some assumption had to be added. About 50 were false, and this is no wonder. Gödel himself, when rereading his notes, would occasionally add a marginal remark: falsch! [incorrect] or schlecht! [bad].”

Von Plato added: “I am sure that the continued study of Gödel’s manuscripts will reveal further treasures. The workbooks contain, Claude says, more than a dozen themes in logic and foundations of mathematics that have not been found in the 80-plus years since they were written down. So this is one thing to explore. But there are many others. His physics and cosmology notebooks are an unknown territory I plan to start exploring once I am finished with my present logic projects.”

Joel David Hamkins, a professor of logic at the University of Notre Dame, Indiana, has not seen Claude’s reconstruction of Gödel’s proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, but said that if it stood up “it is remarkable and historically interesting. Although how much is Claude and how much is Gödel is a job for the historians.”

Hamkins said: “The fact that there are things in there that resemble [Cohen’s proof] does not mean he had it. It shows he was on the path. You don’t get credit for work you don’t tell anyone about. But Gödel had so many ground-breaking ideas that it is maybe not surprising that his notebooks are full of exciting things.”
items.body_ko:
쿠르트 괴델은 1,009페이지 분량의 빽빽하게 쓰인 글을 남겼는데, 그 중 상당 부분은 현재는 사용되지 않는 속기법으로 작성되었으며, 현재 수백 개의 증명된 정리가 포함되어 있다고 합니다.

오스트리아의 논리학자 쿠르트 괴델은 20세기에서 가장 독창적인 사상가 중 한 명입니다. 1931년에 발표된 그의 두 가지 불완전성 정리는 수학을 변화시키고 디지털 시대를 위한 길을 열었습니다.

1930년대의 중요한 결과 이후, 괴델은 몇 편의 논문만을 발표했습니다. 그러나 그의 미발표 작업은 수만 페이지에 달하며 과학사학자들에게 큰 관심을 받고 있습니다.

2017년부터 핀란드 논리학자 얀 폰 플라토는 헬싱키 대학에서 괴델이 1940년대 초에 쓴 16권의 노트를 이해하기 위한 프로젝트를 이끌었습니다. 이 자료인 '워크북'은 수학과 논리에 대한 1,009페이지 분량의 빽빽하게 쓰인 텍스트입니다. 대부분은 괴델이 사용하던 당시에도 이미 사용되지 않던 독일어 속기법인 Gabelsberger로 쓰여 있습니다.

텍스트의 수학적 이해 진전은 고통스러울 정도로 느려서 주당 약 한 페이지 정도였습니다. 그러다 9월에 폰 플라토는 AI 모델 Claude의 도움을 얻었습니다. 이틀 만에 Claude는 전체 자료에 대한 포괄적인 요약을 제공했고, 괴델이 아무도 몰랐던 수백 개의 정리를 증명했다는 사실을 밝혀냈습니다.

현대 시대의 가장 유명한 논리학자는 사실 그 누구도 생각했던 것보다 훨씬 더 많은 것을 발견했습니다.

items.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
items.body: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice. We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on visual question answering and language benchmarks at matched lifetime compute. We find that the visual prior is not necessary; an encoder trained jointly from scratch is on par with a pretrained one, without a separate training stage. What matters instead is dedicated vision capacity: an encoder-free model trails on visual understanding even when its backbone is enlarged by the encoder's parameter count. Yet that capacity need not precede multimodal fusion, as vision-only modules added in-fusion to early backbone layers perform comparably to a pre-fusion encoder and can lower time to first token. These results also hold across backbone sizes, when encoder pretraining is treated as free, and when starting from a pretrained language model. Overall, our findings favor dedicated vision capacity trained jointly with the backbone and placed early within it.

items.title: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research
items.body: Model architecture shapes the scaling behavior, training efficiency, and inference cost of LLMs, making it a central focus of both industry and academia. In industry, teams such as those behind DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi routinely introduce architectural innovations, yet public reports rarely document which ideas succeeded, which were abandoned, and why. In academia, limited compute and inconsistent baselines often restrict evaluations to small-scale, single-point comparisons, making it difficult to establish whether improvements hold at larger scales or translate into broader impact. ArchSpace addresses both gaps as a public platform for Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing Architecture Researc}: each proposal is recorded with its experiments and reasoning, reviewed by the community, and referenced by later work. To evaluate ideas before costly large-scale training, ArchSpace leverages scaling laws to predict model loss at larger scales from smaller experiments, a practice widely adopted in industry. We provide initial references that make the platform usable: Qwen3.5 and OLMo3 baselines, fitted scaling laws, and a reusable training recipe. Ideas validated through this review can in turn become new baselines, and ArchSpace thereby aims to broaden the range of ideas that shape the next generation of models.
