items.title: Primer: An AI Framework for Instructor-Centered Educational Simulation Creation
items.body: Educational simulations are a well-established pedagogical technique that gives learners opportunities to apply knowledge, respond to challenges, and reflect on their performance. High-quality simulations, however, are difficult to build, requiring instructor input, scenario design, character development, scaffolding, technical implementation, and repeated revision. This paper presents Primer, an open-source, LLM-agnostic AI-supported system that helps educators create adaptive educational simulations. Educators contribute their knowledge of the subject, lesson, and students, while generative AI produces responsive variations of practice for students. Primer uses a multi-agent system centered around executing educator's instructional intent through the entire learning experience. We hope that by releasing Primer as an open-source system, including its prompts and GitHub repository, we provide a foundation for development and research on educator-in-the-loop AI authoring, multi-agent educational workflows, and simulation-based pedagogy. Further, by allowing the use of various AI models, including local and open source models, we provide the opportunity for implementation under varied governance regimes. Primer points toward a model of educational AI in which instructors can create locally grounded practice opportunities based on their own materials, goals, examples, and knowledge of students.
items.title_ko: 강사 중심의 교육 시뮬레이션 제작을 돕는 AI 프레임워크 Primer 공개
items.summary_ko: Primer는 교사들이 복잡한 교육 시뮬레이션을 쉽게 만들 수 있도록 지원하는 오픈소스 AI 시스템입니다. 이 시스템은 LLM에 구애받지 않고 시나리오 설계, 캐릭터 개발, 맞춤형 학습 지원 등 시뮬레이션 제작의 여러 단계를 돕습니다.

items.title: ElasticDino: Dense Semantic Features Using Elastic Deformations
items.body: Vision transformers (ViTs) serve as the backbone for countless vision tasks, including dense prediction tasks, such as segmentation and depth estimation, even though the quadratic complexity of self-attention severely limits feature resolution and induces spatial artifacts. In this work, we introduce ElasticDino, a lightweight adapter which produces high-resolution feature maps, adhering to the fine details of the input image. As a key insight, we observe the consistency of artifacts across channels, and simultaneously resolve them to match the input image structure. Using a slim architecture based on spatial deformations, ElasticDino produces pixel-aligned, high-resolution feature maps efficiently. Leveraging deformations allows strictly preserving sharp semantics, and thereby avoiding the smoothness biases inherent to alternative approaches. Due to the absence of ground truth, we employ pixel-level semantic segmentation and depth estimation with linear heads to predict a set of downstream dense tasks, guiding the deformation process without leaking task-specific semantics into the model. We demonstrate superior accuracy over current methods on a range of popular dense task benchmarks, with better computational performance.
items.body_ko: Vision Transformer(ViT)는 분할(segmentation) 및 깊이 추정(depth estimation)과 같은 고밀도 예측(dense prediction) 작업을 포함하여 수많은 비전 작업의 기반 역할을 하지만, Self-attention의 2차 복잡도는 특징 해상도(feature resolution)를 심각하게 제한하고 공간적 아티팩트를 유발합니다. 본 연구에서는 입력 이미지의 미세한 디테일을 준수하는 고해상도 특징 맵을 생성하는 경량 어댑터인 ElasticDino를 소개합니다. 핵심 통찰력으로, 채널 전반에 걸쳐 아티팩트의 일관성을 관찰하고, 동시에 이를 해결하여 입력 이미지 구조와 일치시킵니다. 공간 변형(spatial deformations)을 기반으로 하는 슬림한 아키텍처를 사용하여 ElasticDino는 픽셀 정렬된 고해상도 특징 맵을 효율적으로 생성합니다. 변형을 활용하면 날카로운 의미론을 엄격하게 보존하여 대체 접근 방식에 내재된 평활화 편향(smoothness biases)을 피할 수 있습니다. Ground Truth의 부재로 인해, 우리는 픽셀 수준의 Semantic Segmentation 및 Depth Estimation을 선형 헤드와 함께 사용하여 일련의 다운스트림 고밀도 작업을 예측하고, 작업별 의미론이 모델로 유출되지 않도록 변형 프로세스를 안내합니다. 우리는 현재 방법보다 우수한 정확도를 다양한 인기 고밀도 작업 벤치마크에서 더 나은 계산 성능으로 입증합니다.
items.title_ko: Vision Transformer의 밀집 특징 해상도를 높이는 ElasticDino 소개
items.summary_ko: ElasticDino는 Vision Transformer(ViT)의 밀집 예측 작업(예: 분할, 깊이 추정)에서 발생하는 해상도 제한 및 공간 아티팩트를 개선하는 경량 어댑터입니다. 이 기술은 입력 이미지의 세부 사항을 잘 포착하는 고해상도 특징 맵을 생성하며, 채널 전반의 아티팩트 일관성 관찰에서 핵심적인 아이디어를 얻었습니다.
items.why_ko: ViT 기반의 컴퓨터 비전 모델이 고해상도 이미지 처리에서 겪는 성능 저하 문제를 해결하여, 정밀한 시각 인식 애플리케이션 개발에 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Compiling Known Rules into Compact Neural Agents: Weight-Space Programming on Unseen Games
items.body: Weight-space programming (WSP) uses language models to construct neural network weights without training. We test whether known game mechanics can be compiled into compact agents that generalise to held-out levels, renderings and start states within a game family. Writers receive simulator source with held-out level data removed for 20 privately authored, unpublished ARC-AGI-3-style game families. With a fixed 57k-parameter recurrent architecture, the strongest writer reaches 56% held-out-level success with feedback, while the four main writers' Python players reach 97-100%. An exploratory free-architecture condition reaches 68-90%. Learning from support-level examples transfers much less well, but these learners lack the source information given to writers. Written networks have a program-like structure: 93% of parameters are zero, and 90% of the rest are small integers or powers of two. NumPy players under comparable computation caps reach 91%, versus the networks' 79%. Training the strongest writer's architectures from scratch yields about 1% success within our budget. Written fixed-network weights are fragile, and standard PPO removes most of their success. Prompts for noise robustness increase tolerance by about four orders of magnitude for two of three writers, but PPO makes larger updates and still removes most success. These results demonstrate rule-to-network compilation in this setting, while showing limited benefits over Python programs and no successful combination with the tested PPO fine-tuning.
items.title_ko: 언어 모델로 게임 규칙을 컴파일하여 새로운 게임에 적용하는 기술 연구
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 언어 모델을 활용하여 학습 없이 신경망 가중치를 구성하는 '가중치 공간 프로그래밍(Weight-space programming, WSP)' 기법을 다룹니다. 알려진 게임 규칙을 57k 매개변수 순환 아키텍처를 가진 에이전트에 컴파일하여, 낯선 레벨, 렌더링, 시작 상태의 게임 가족에 대해 56%의 일반화 성능을 달성했습니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 학습 없이 게임 규칙을 이해하고 새로운 환경에 적용하는 능력을 보여주어, 제로샷 일반화와 효율적인 에이전트 개발 가능성을 제시합니다.

items.title: Morphological Simplification in Alzheimer's Disease: Computational Analysis and Identification From Connected Speech
items.body:
Purpose: Morphology is often regarded as relatively spared in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and is rarely modeled in connected speech. This study asked which morphological features distinguish speakers with AD from healthy controls, how well morphology classifies AD compared with other linguistic levels and BERT-based models, and whether the signal exceeds transcript length and vocabulary. Method: Fifty-five automatic measures in eight families, seven of them new and theory-motivated, were computed from participant speech in the ADReSS Cookie Theft descriptions (78 AD, 78 controls) and analyzed with group comparisons, equivalence tests, SHAP, family ablation, likelihood-ratio tests, feature-selection classifiers, and BERT-based models. The automatic measures were validated manually, and models were transferred to two other corpora. Results: Nineteen of 38 measures differed between groups: speakers with AD produced fewer suffixed and inflected words, shorter verbs and nouns, and fewer present-progressive but more past-tense forms (largest effect r = -0.42), whereas errors were rare and statistically equivalent between groups. Eight measures survived adjustment for length and lexical frequency. With test-set feature selection, morphology reached a macro-F1 of 0.85, on par with syntax and above fine-tuned BERT (0.80 over five seeds); fully cross-validated selection gave 0.62. Adding morphology to BERT improved AUC (0.91 vs. 0.89) but not macro-F1. Transfer was limited, although two thirds of the effects kept their direction in mild cognitive impairment. Conclusions: AD connected speech shows morphological simplification and temporal reanchoring rather than breakdown. Morphology is more informative than its reputation suggests.
Keywords: Alzheimer's disease; morphology; connected speech; ADReSS; inflection; tense and aspect; SHAP; machine learning; BERT

items.title: The Value of Thinking: Learning When to Reason in Hybrid Decision Models
items.body: Existing adaptive-reasoning methods shorten the explicit reasoning a model writes, or skip it by switching modes; either way the answer is still written out token by token. \emph{Rather than deciding how much to think}, we explore a different paradigm, \emph{zero-or-$T$ thinking}: a single model either answers from the implicit thinking inside one forward pass, generating no token, or performs full autoregressive reasoning at a cost of $T$ tokens when that is worth paying. We realise it in a \emph{hybrid decision model} (HDM), where one frozen backbone serves both modes and a lightweight \emph{self-routing block} chooses between them. The block estimates the \emph{value of thinking}, the utility the slow mode is expected to add over the fast one, from what that implicit thinking has already produced, and the slow mode runs only where that value exceeds a price $λ$ set per request. Where no per-decision label exists, as in episodic agentic tasks, we introduce \emph{Calibrated Decision Policy Optimisation} (CDPO), a reinforcement-learning recipe that trains the block from episode-level returns. We evaluate HDM on MMLU-Pro, AGIEval, GPQA-Diamond, JevBench, BANKING77 and MiniWoB. Specifically, on JevBench HDM-4B scores $0.857$ against Jev's $0.851$ ($+0.7\%$) at a median $0.179$\,s against $0.652$ ($-72.5\%$). On the agentic venue MiniWoB HDM-27B cuts token cost by $80.1\%$.
items.title_ko: 하이브리드 의사결정 모델에서 '생각' 여부를 결정하는 새로운 패러다임 제안
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 기존의 적응적 추론 방식과 달리, 모델이 명시적인 추론을 수행할지('T 토큰을 소비하여 완전한 자기회귀 추론') 아니면 단일 순방향 패스 내의 암묵적 사고만으로 답변할지('0 토큰 소비')를 결정하는 '0 또는 T 사고' 패러다임을 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 추론 비용과 효율성 사이의 균형을 최적화하는 새로운 방법을 제시하여, 자원 제약이 있는 환경에서 AI 모델의 실용성을 높일 수 있습니다.

items.title: Lara Mini Base: Language Diversity as a Resource, Not a Trade-off
items.body: General-purpose language models are trained mostly on English: over open models we review, at most, non-English pretraining data makes up only a 12% share. Models built for European languages give them far more, but score well below general-purpose models of the same size. A common concern is that, in small models, languages compete for capacity. We present Lara Mini base, a model trained from scratch on 6T tokens in English and 44 other languages, which together cover all 24 official languages of the European Union. As training progresses, the 44 other languages together come to outweigh English. To give these languages enough capacity at low cost, Lara Mini base uses a mixture of experts architecture with 7.2B total and 0.6B active parameters. Among open base models with up to 2B active parameters, it achieves the highest average score across standard English, multilingual, math, and code benchmarks, ahead of models trained on 4 to 6 times as many tokens. Its margin is largest on multilingual benchmarks in the languages it supports and on math benchmarks. It supports contexts of up to 128k tokens. We find that our MoE architecture reduces capacity competition between languages. For a single user on one GPU, without quantization, it generates text at least 1.8 times faster than any model with a higher average score. We release the weights of Lara Mini base under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license. In addition, we will release T-HellaSwag, a higher-quality machine translation of the commonsense reasoning benchmark HellaSwag into 110 language variants.
items.body_ko: 범용 언어 모델은 대부분 영어로 학습됩니다. 우리가 검토한 오픈 모델 중 비영어권 사전 학습 데이터는 최대 12%에 불과합니다. 유럽 언어를 위해 구축된 모델은 훨씬 더 많은 데이터를 사용하지만, 동일한 크기의 범용 모델보다 훨씬 낮은 점수를 기록합니다. 일반적인 우려는 작은 모델에서 언어들이 용량 경쟁을 한다는 것입니다. 우리는 영어와 44개의 다른 언어로 된 6T 토큰으로 처음부터 학습된 모델인 Lara Mini base를 소개합니다. 이 44개의 언어는 유럽 연합의 24개 공식 언어를 모두 포함합니다. 학습이 진행됨에 따라 44개의 다른 언어가 영어보다 중요해집니다. 이러한 언어에 낮은 비용으로 충분한 용량을 제공하기 위해 Lara Mini base는 총 7.2B 및 활성 0.6B 매개변수를 가진 전문가 혼합(mixture of experts) 아키텍처를 사용합니다. 활성 매개변수 2B 이하의 오픈 기반 모델 중에서, 이는 표준 영어, 다국어, 수학 및 코드 벤치마크 전반에서 가장 높은 평균 점수를 달성하며, 4~6배 더 많은 토큰으로 학습된 모델보다 앞서 있습니다. 이 모델의 가장 큰 차이는 지원하는 언어의 다국어 벤치마크와 수학 벤치마크에서 나타납니다. 최대 128k 토큰의 컨텍스트를 지원합니다. 우리는 MoE 아키텍처가 언어 간의 용량 경쟁을 줄인다는 것을 발견했습니다. 양자화 없이 단일 GPU를 사용하는 단일 사용자에게는 평균 점수가 더 높은 어떤 모델보다 최소 1.8배 빠르게 텍스트를 생성합니다. 우리는 Lara Mini base의 가중치를 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 라이선스 하에 공개합니다. 또한, 상식 추론 벤치마크 HellaSwag을 110개 언어 변형으로 더 높은 품질의 기계 번역한 T-HellaSwag을 공개할 예정입니다.
items.title_ko: 다언어 능력을 향상시킨 소형 언어 모델 'Lara Mini Base' 발표
items.summary_ko: Lara Mini base는 6조 개의 토큰으로 영어와 44개 언어(유럽 연합 24개 공용어 포함)를 학습하여, 언어 다양성이 모델 용량 경쟁으로 이어지지 않도록 설계되었습니다. 기존 소형 다언어 모델이 영어 중심 모델에 비해 성능이 낮았던 한계를 극복하고, 언어 간 용량 경쟁 우려를 해소했습니다.
items.why_ko: 적은 리소스로도 다양한 언어를 효율적으로 처리하는 소형 LLM 개발의 가능성을 열어, 다국어 지원 애플리케이션 개발에 큰 도움이 될 것입니다.

items.title: S1-Evo: Experience-Guided Evidence Competition Attacks on Typed System-1 Decision Models
items.body: Typed System-1 (S1) decision models are increasingly deployed in LLM agents for routing, moderation, and authorization to cut inference cost, yet untrusted context can still manipulate typed outputs and alter execution branches. Unlike autoregressive System-2 (S2) models, S1 interfaces score dynamic rules and options without token-by-token decoding, mismatching attacks targeting text continuation or explicit override commands. We propose S1-Evo, a self-evolving framework tailored to S1's contract-based option competition and margin feedback. S1-Evo perturbs untrusted fields via contract-aware evidence channels to induce \emph{evidence competition} with original task evidence while preserving fact invariance. Offline on seed tasks, it optimizes candidates via feedback search guided by directional margins and re-verification, distilling verified flips into experience cards. At test time, S1-Evo retrieves relevant cards to construct perturbations for unseen tasks. Across four benchmarks and three S1 models, S1-Evo reaches 71.99\% mean ASR and 57.47\% high-confidence ASR on \texttt{jev-1.14}, and causes up to 24.00\% E2E agent violations.
items.title_ko: System-1 의사결정 모델에 대한 새로운 공격 프레임워크 'S1-Evo' 제안
items.summary_ko: S1-Evo는 LLM 에이전트의 라우팅, 중재, 권한 부여에 사용되는 System-1(S1) 의사결정 모델을 대상으로 하는 자체 진화 프레임워크입니다. S1 모델은 추론 비용 절감을 위해 토큰별 디코딩 없이 동적 규칙과 옵션을 평가하므로, 텍스트 연속성이나 명시적 재정의 명령을 목표로 하는 기존 공격 방식과는 다르게 작동합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트의 보안 취약성을 이해하고 개선하는 데 필수적인 연구로, 새로운 형태의 공격에 대한 방어 전략 개발에 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Universal Infectious Disease Forecasting with Mantis 2
items.body:
Public health agencies need to anticipate how outbreaks will unfold, when they will peak, and how long demand on health services will remain elevated. We previously developed a foundation model, Mantis, which was trained entirely on simulated outbreaks---enabling us to generate the diversity and scale of training data needed to support forecasting across diseases. However, our previous work left unresolved when simulation improves predictions and how it should complement observational data.
Here, we varied the balance of simulated and observed training data while holding forecasting tasks fixed and varying the available surveillance history. We found that simulation-rich training was particularly valuable with limited local history, and its relative advantage diminished as more observations became available. We also found that simulation-based training reduced exceptionally large forecast errors, suggesting that mechanistic knowledge can help compensate for limited local evidence.
Building on these findings, we developed Mantis 2, which combines simulated and observational training to jointly forecast up to six variables sixteen weeks ahead. Across 30 forecasting tasks, Mantis 2 achieved the best aggregate probabilistic accuracy over short, medium, and long horizons among the machine learning, statistical, and baseline models evaluated. It missed roughly 30\% fewer outbreak peaks than the strongest comparison model, with successfully anticipated peaks identified more than six weeks in advance on average. We publicly release Mantis 2, enabling public health agencies and researchers to forecast disease outcomes without developing a separate model for each disease or location.
items.title_ko: 시뮬레이션 기반 범용 전염병 예측 모델 'Mantis 2' 개발
items.summary_ko: Mantis 2는 모의 전염병 데이터를 활용하여 훈련된 범용 예측 모델 Mantis의 후속 버전입니다. 이 모델은 다양한 질병에 걸쳐 발병 추이를 예측하고, 최고점 시기 및 의료 서비스 수요 지속 기간을 전망하는 데 활용됩니다. 특히 시뮬레이션 데이터가 예측 개선에 언제 어떻게 기여하는지, 그리고 관측 데이터와 어떻게 보완되어야 하는지에 대한 통찰을 제공합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 기반 전염병 예측 모델은 공중 보건 기관의 대응 능력을 강화하고, 팬데믹 관리 및 자원 배분에 중요한 정보를 제공할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Time Flies When You Parallelise: Pareto-efficient Time Series Foundation Models with Linear Recurrences
items.body: Time series foundation models have demonstrated strong zero-shot forecasting performance, but computational efficiency remains a central architectural challenge. Temporal self-attention incurs quadratic cost in the number of temporal tokens, while nonlinear recurrent state transitions restrict parallel computation along the temporal dimension. We introduce ci-proto, a family of time series foundation models based on Mamba-3, whose linear state recurrences support chunk-wise parallel-in-time computation during training, and inference costs that scale linearly with sequence length. The architecture alternates recurrent temporal processing with cross-variate attention, supporting multivariate probabilistic forecasting with past-only and future-known covariates. Across fev-bench's 100 forecasting tasks, ci-proto XL sets a new state of the art among time series foundation models. The five ci-proto variants also make up the entire Pareto frontier for mean scaled quantile loss and mean absolute scaled error against both parameter count and median runtime.
items.body_ko: 시계열 파운데이션 모델은 강력한 제로샷 예측 성능을 보여주었지만, 계산 효율성은 여전히 핵심적인 아키텍처 과제로 남아 있습니다. 시간적 Self-Attention은 시간 토큰 수에 따라 2차 비용을 발생시키고, 비선형 순환 상태 전이는 시간 차원을 따라 병렬 계산을 제한합니다. 우리는 Mamba-3를 기반으로 한 시계열 파운데이션 모델 제품군인 ci-proto를 소개합니다. ci-proto의 선형 상태 순환은 훈련 중 청크 단위의 시간 병렬 계산을 지원하며, 추론 비용은 시퀀스 길이에 따라 선형적으로 확장됩니다. 이 아키텍처는 순환 시간 처리와 교차 변량 Attention을 번갈아 사용하여, 과거 전용 및 미래를 아는 공변량을 포함한 다변량 확률적 예측을 지원합니다. fev-bench의 100가지 예측 작업 전반에서 ci-proto XL은 시계열 파운데이션 모델 중 새로운 최첨단 기록을 세웠습니다. 또한, 5가지 ci-proto 변형은 매개변수 수와 중간 런타임 모두에 대해 평균 스케일드 분위수 손실(mean scaled quantile loss) 및 평균 절대 스케일드 오차(mean absolute scaled error)에 대한 전체 파레토 프론티어(Pareto frontier)를 구성합니다.
items.title_ko: 선형 순환을 활용한 시계열 파운데이션 모델 'ci-proto' 발표
items.summary_ko: ci-proto는 Mamba-3를 기반으로 하는 시계열 파운데이션 모델군으로, 시간 차원에서 청크별 병렬 계산을 지원하는 선형 상태 순환을 특징으로 합니다. 이 모델은 시간적 자기 주의의 이차적 비용과 비선형 순환 상태 전이의 병렬 계산 제약이라는 기존 시계열 모델의 효율성 문제를 해결합니다.
items.why_ko: 시계열 데이터 처리의 계산 효율성을 크게 향상시켜, 대규모 시계열 데이터 기반의 예측 및 분석 모델 개발에 새로운 가능성을 제시합니다.

items.title: Kezek: Splitting Mono Two-Person Conversations into Per-Speaker Tracks for Full-Duplex Dialogue Data
items.body: Full-duplex spoken dialogue models learn turn-taking, overlaps and backchannels from conversations recorded with one channel per speaker, but most available conversational audio is a single mono mix. We present Kezek, a model that turns a mono recording of exactly two people into one track per person with the original length and timing; overlaps and short replies ("yeah", "mm-hm") stay on the track of the person who said them. Kezek decides who speaks when and who is who once for the whole recording (stage 1: a two-voice activity model guided by a speaker fingerprint trained to be insensitive to phase), and a conditioned time-domain separator only carries out that decision (stage 2), with outputs that always sum to the input. Standard separation metrics miss the failures that matter for dialogue data, so we report short-reply retention, leakage onto the other person's solo, channel swaps and coverage. Against the open pipeline pyannote -> DialogueSidon on the same recordings, Kezek keeps more short replies (0.83 vs. 0.69 on Open Yap test; 0.80 vs. 0.71 over the other's speech on unseen telephone speech from CallHome English), mostly because it returns the whole recording while the external pipeline drops part of it (on the audio both return, reply retention is about the same: 0.859 vs. 0.865 on Open Yap); it also leaks less, swaps channels less often, and runs 4-5 times faster (about 230 hours of audio per GPU-hour). We also report negative results and an ideal-mask ceiling that locate the remaining gap: quiet replies under a louder voice. Code and weights are released under permissive licences.
items.title_ko: 모노 대화를 화자별 트랙으로 분리하는 모델 'Kezek' 개발
items.summary_ko: Kezek은 두 사람의 모노 대화 녹음을 각 화자별 트랙으로 분리하여, 원래 길이와 타이밍을 유지하면서 대화 오버랩과 짧은 응답도 각 화자 트랙에 정확히 배치하는 모델입니다. 이 모델은 전체 녹음에서 누가 언제 말했는지, 누가 누구인지 한 번만 결정합니다.
items.why_ko: 단일 채널 녹음에서 풀-듀플렉스 대화 데이터를 생성하여, 대화형 AI 모델 학습을 위한 데이터 부족 문제를 해결하고 상호작용성 높은 AI 개발에 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: SPADE: Soft Prompts for Ai-text DEtection
items.body: The easy access to Large Language Models (LLMs) has made AI-generated texts on the web increasingly ubiquitous, making AI-text detection a crucial task. Prompts greatly influence the generation process, but existing detectors focus solely on the generated texts --- supervised methods learn from labeled texts only, and zero-shot methods rely on the text's probability distributions --- ignoring the underlying generation process, which limits their robustness in open-world scenarios. We introduce SPADE: Soft Prompts for Ai-text DEtection, a novel framework for detecting AI-generated text that transfers better across datasets. Specifically, we measure the prompt's influence and use it as a discriminative signal. We characterize the prompt's influence by introducing a Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) term that captures how much a prompt explains a text. Based on this quantity, SPADE trains one soft prompt per class to amplify the separation, and predicts the class whose prompt best explains the candidate text. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks against various detectors demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our method, achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on out-of-distribution (OOD) datasets.
items.title_ko: AI 생성 텍스트 감지를 위한 'Soft Prompts(SPADE)' 기법 제안
items.summary_ko: SPADE는 LLM 생성 텍스트 탐지를 위해 프롬프트를 활용하는 새로운 접근 방식을 제안합니다. 기존 탐지기가 텍스트 자체에만 집중했던 것과 달리, 이 기법은 생성 과정에 영향을 미치는 프롬프트 정보를 활용하여 개방형 시나리오에서 탐지 견고성을 높입니다.
items.why_ko: AI 생성 콘텐츠가 확산되는 상황에서, AI 텍스트 탐지기의 신뢰성과 강건성을 높여 AI 오용 문제를 해결하는 데 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: STEALTH: Steganographic Text Encoding Agnostic to Low-Level Tensor Hardware
items.body: Provably secure linguistic steganography hides a message inside text sampled from a language model, so that without the key, a stegotext is computationally indistinguishable from an honest model sample. Nearly every such scheme assumes the receiver can recompute the sender's token probabilities exactly bit for bit. We show this assumption is fragile: across three model families, bit-exact schemes decode almost none of our messages once the receiver's floating-point precision, quantization, or GPU architecture differs from the sender's, or even when the receiver merely scores a text in parallel versus one token at a time, with the same model, precision, and hardware held fixed. We present STEALTH, a scheme built for exactly this setting. The sender draws each token with an exponential race driven by keyed pseudorandom noise, so a receiver's probability mismatch flips a token only when the race is close; a rateless spinal code, decoded by beam search, absorbs the resulting flips without the sender and receiver ever agreeing on a single distribution. We prove stegotexts remain indistinguishable from honest samples under this construction. Empirically, STEALTH decodes every message we sent for every receiver in the sender's model family, at every precision and quantization level, on smaller models, and on a different GPU architecture. STEALTH is even robust across different model families with separate vocabularies and tokenizers, decoding every message we tested. Our approach carries far more payload per token than prior robust schemes, and trained steganalyzers and a targeted statistical test both fail to distinguish its stegotexts from honest model output.

items.title: Beyond Word Error Rate: A Failure Taxonomy of Streaming Dictation ASR
items.body: Speech recognition (ASR) systems are usually compared by word error rate (WER) on recorded files, after punctuation, capital letters and number format are removed. In dictation, the audio is streamed live and the text goes into the user's message as written, so what matters is which mistakes the user has to fix. The test set, streamed to eleven ASR systems, comprises 106 scripted English dictations from one speaker (read in a quiet room, with a fan on, and whispered), 20 clips in each of eleven other language and dialect sets, and 400 recordings that join clips in two languages. Every error was sorted by a fixed rule into four levels: recognition, output formatting, language handling and, for the self-hosted models, audio dropped before the model. Systems with similar WER failed in different ways. Zoom Scribe and OpenAI's GPT-Live-Transcribe have almost the same WER on quiet English (7.4% and 7.3%), but 34.7% and 8.8% on whispered English. Zoom and both AssemblyAI models left out 26-28% of whispered words, and still 21-26% with their end-of-turn detection relaxed or off; seven other systems left out at most 3%. Qwen3-ASR's 32% came from the speech detection in our own deployment (6% when relaxed). Across 107 EARS speakers, the same four systems lost 7-31% of whispered words, while six others lost under 2%. With only English selected, Gemini, Deepgram and our self-hosted Whisper lost the non-English part of a two-language recording in 86-99% of recordings, against 33-46% with both languages selected, while GPT-Live-Transcribe, OpenAI's realtime Whisper and Meta lost it in at most 20%. Running Whisper behind a Silero voice activity detector that drops audio judged to be silence raised whispered WER from 10.1% to 51.4%. Most English results come from one read speaker. The code, the recordings, both references and every transcript are released.
items.title_ko: 실시간 받아쓰기 ASR 시스템 오류 분류 체계 제안
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 실시간 받아쓰기 ASR(자동 음성 인식) 시스템의 성능을 평가할 때, 기존의 단어 오류율(WER) 대신 사용자가 수정해야 하는 실수를 중심으로 하는 새로운 오류 분류 체계를 제안합니다. 다양한 환경(조용한 방, 팬 소음, 속삭임)에서 11개 ASR 시스템을 테스트하여, WER이 받아쓰기 성능을 완전히 반영하지 못함을 보여줍니다.
items.why_ko: 실제 사용자 경험에 기반한 ASR 평가 기준을 제시하여, 받아쓰기 기능의 실용적인 개선과 개발에 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: CADET: Construction of PCB Routing Instances with Executable Demonstrations
items.body: Printed circuit board (PCB) routing is the stage of physical layout that finds paths connecting the placed pads of each net. Public datasets in this domain are few, and most contain only the final states of routed boards, not demonstrations of the electronic design automation (EDA) engine actions that produce them. To close this gap, we propose CADET (Constructing executAble Demonstrations for Engine-grounded Training), which jointly generates synthetic boards and demonstrations built from EDA engine actions. The resulting RouteDemos provides 100,000 synthetic boards routed with zero design rule violations (DRVs), together with their demonstrations. Their distributions over 17 statistics resemble those of 142 real reference boards. CADET trains a routing policy on these demonstrations with behavior cloning and fine-tunes it with reinforcement learning (RL). On real test boards, the policy raised the rate of complete DRV-free routing from 38.0% to 67.2% over an RL-only baseline. This rate was comparable to that of the open-source autorouter FreeRouting and exceeded those of the other baselines, including GPT-6 Astra. We release the dataset and its generation code as open source at https://github.com/LGAI-Research/CADET.
items.title_ko: PCB 라우팅 인스턴스 생성을 위한 CADET 프레임워크 제안
items.summary_ko: CADET(Constructing executAble Demonstrations for Engine-grounded Training)는 인쇄회로기판(PCB) 라우팅을 위한 합성 보드와 EDA(전자 설계 자동화) 엔진 동작 데모를 동시에 생성하는 프레임워크입니다. 기존 공개 데이터셋이 라우팅 완료 상태만 제공하고 생성 과정을 보여주지 않는 한계를 극복합니다.
items.why_ko: PCB 설계 자동화 분야에서 모델 학습을 위한 풍부한 데이터셋과 실행 가능한 데모를 제공하여, AI 기반 EDA 툴 개발에 중요한 기반을 마련합니다.

items.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
items.body: Second-order optimizers (e.g., Shampoo, SOAP) have emerged as compelling alternatives to Adam/AdamW and promise faster per-step convergence than AdamW in transformer training. However, they still remain costly in practice, and even SOAP still pays substantial optimizer-state memory and eigendecomposition overhead. We ask whether the benefits of SOAP can be retained at nearly the efficiency of AdamW. In this paper, we answer yes with a lightweight SOAP variant, Factored One-sided Adam-Moment (FOAM). The path to practical impact is twofold: first, FOAM employs input-only preconditioning, dropping the output-side Kronecker factor to reduce memory and remove one eigendecomposition. The Kronecker structure of the Hessian shows that this is exact for a diagonal output-side curvature and nearly lossless for a near-diagonal one, as we observe empirically. Second, FOAM replaces SOAP's dense rotated second moment with a factored Adam-moment estimator based on row-by-column statistics. Under the K-FAC Fisher assumption with a diagonal output curvature, this estimator exactly recovers SOAP's dense second moment, and we measure only a 15-20% K-FAC violation, with negligible effect on the update. Our empirical results support the claim that FOAM matches strong SOAP and Muon baselines in validation loss across scales of large language model (LLM) pre-training, uses half of SOAP's optimizer state, runs at Muon-class wall-clock time, and retains robustness across a three-fold learning-rate range. The results hold from 124M to 760M parameters, demonstrating that SOAP's gains need not require SOAP's cost. Code: https://github.com/naver-ai/foam

items.title: Uncertainty-aware quantum machine learning based on Dempster-Shafer theory
items.body: A large body of work in quantum machine learning has centered on characterizing the expressivity and performance of quantum models. In contrast, little attention has been paid to the reliability of predictions beyond average performance measures such as accuracy. In this work, we introduce an uncertainty-aware quantum classification framework based on Dempster-Shafer theory. This theory allows to express uncertainty through weights assigned not only to individual classification labels but to sets of labels. We introduce a training strategy that enables parameterized quantum circuits to learn such assignments directly from data. This provides an efficient way to prepare the corresponding quantum states and enables the application of different post-processing strategies. In particular, it offers a practical setting for quantum Dempster-Shafer fusion procedures with polynomial resource requirements, even when the corresponding mass functions are defined over exponentially many subsets. Overall, our work represents a step toward enabling quantum models to express uncertainty about their predictions, thereby extending the evaluation of quantum models beyond predictive performance alone.
items.title_ko: 불확실성을 고려한 양자 머신러닝 프레임워크 제안
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 Dempster-Shafer 이론을 기반으로 불확실성을 고려하는 양자 분류 프레임워크를 소개합니다. 개별 분류 레이블뿐만 아니라 레이블 집합에도 가중치를 할당하여 불확실성을 표현함으로써, 모델의 평균적인 성능 지표를 넘어 예측의 신뢰성을 평가합니다.
items.why_ko: 양자 머신러닝 모델의 예측 신뢰도를 높여, 의료나 금융과 같이 불확실성 관리가 중요한 분야에서 양자 AI의 적용 가능성을 확대합니다.

items.title: Human or Synthetic? What a Fixed Budget Buys for Post-Training
items.body: Post-training of large language models typically combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with preference-based fine-tuning such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). Human-annotated and synthetically generated preference data differ substantially in per-sample cost, but prior work typically holds sample count fixed when comparing the two. In this work, we explicitly study the interplay between cost and performance by comparing the effect of post-training with human and synthetic preference data under a fixed, dollar-matched annotation budget. We train and evaluate multiple base model families across helpfulness and summarization tasks. We find that synthetic data is far more cost-efficient at low-to-moderate budgets, achieving high win rates with as little as \$200--\$400. On helpfulness, human data closes the gap only at budgets roughly two orders of magnitude larger; on summarization, it does not close the gap at any tested budget. We also find that human-annotated data varies in reliability: one widely used human preference source substantially underperforms another, and the gap persists even after standard remedies such as domain restriction and deduplication.
items.title_ko: LLM 후처리 학습에서 인간 데이터와 합성 데이터의 비용 효율성 비교 연구
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 LLM의 후처리 학습(SFT 및 DPO 등)에서 인간이 주석을 단 선호 데이터와 합성으로 생성된 선호 데이터의 비용 대비 성능을 비교합니다. 기존 연구가 샘플 수를 고정하고 비교했던 것과 달리, 비용과 성능 간의 상호작용을 명확하게 분석했습니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 파인튜닝 시 데이터 소스 선택에 대한 실질적인 가이드라인을 제공하여, 제한된 예산으로 모델 성능을 극대화하는 전략 수립에 도움을 줍니다.

items.title: Look It Up: Multi-bit LLM Watermarking via Codebook Search
items.body: Attributing short LLM-generated texts to a specific source remains challenging for existing multi-bit watermarking methods, which often require long generations or costly decoding to recover payloads reliably. We propose a codebook-based watermarking scheme that maps an $n$-bit payload to a longer $u$-bit codeword and embeds it during generation through token-level logit biasing. During extraction, the received bit sequence is matched to the nearest codeword in a precomputed secret codebook using Hamming or Levenshtein distance. Experiments show that our method achieves near-perfect recovery for 16-24 bit payloads on 200-token generations and strong performance on 127-token generations for base models. Results are weaker on some instruction-tuned models with very short texts, where low-entropy output distributions reduce embedding reliability. We also study a BCH-based variant that avoids codebook storage but generally reduces robustness. The Levenshtein variant improves resilience to deletions and light paraphrasing, while insertions and stronger rewrites remain challenging. We analyze collision probability, codeword separation, extraction time, tokenization consistency, and text quality, highlighting both the practicality and limitations of codebook-based watermarking for short-form attribution.
items.title_ko: 코드북 검색 기반의 다중 비트 LLM 워터마킹 기법 'Look It Up' 제안
items.summary_ko: 'Look It Up'은 LLM 생성 텍스트에 다중 비트 페이로드를 워터마킹하는 새로운 코드북 기반 기법입니다. n-비트 페이로드를 더 긴 u-비트 코드워드로 매핑하고 토큰 수준 로짓 편향을 통해 삽입하며, 추출 시에는 수신된 비트 시퀀스를 사전 계산된 코드북에서 가장 가까운 코드워드와 일치시킵니다.
items.why_ko: 짧은 LLM 생성 텍스트에서도 신뢰성 있는 출처 식별이 가능하게 하여, AI 생성 콘텐츠의 저작권 보호 및 오용 방지 기술 발전에 기여합니다.

items.title: LLM-Assisted Verification in Dafny
items.body: Formal verification of complex algorithms requires expertise in program specification, invariant construction, mathematical proof, and the management of automated theorem provers. Although large language models (LLMs) can generate program code and proof fragments, reliably developing complete machine-checked verifications remains challenging: it requires an iterative process of constructing and validating specifications and invariants, building proofs, diagnosing solver failures, and optimizing verification performance. This paper presents a systematic ten-step workflow for LLM-assisted verification of scientific algorithms using the Dafny verification system. The workflow integrates algorithm formalization, contract development, empirical invariant validation, proof construction, bottleneck profiling, and resource-driven proof optimization. We applied the workflow using Antrhopic's Claude Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 models, combining LLM-driven development with automated testing and verification feedback, while retaining human oversight for correctness-critical decisions and strategic interventions. We evaluate the approach on 37 complex algorithms from graph theory and labelled transition systems. Notably, we verified the Hopfcroft-Tarjan triconnectivity test, demonstrating that even highly challenging algorithmic verification tasks can be carried out through a structured LLM-assisted workflow. Many of our machine-checked verifications were obtained within hours to a few days of interactive development. Our results suggest that LLM-assisted workflows can shift the role of the human verifier from detailed proof construction toward supervision, specification review, and strategic guidance.
items.title_ko: LLM 지원 Dafny 검증: 복잡한 알고리즘의 공식 검증 자동화

items.title: Pretraining Data Statistics Shape the Phases of Learning Entity Comparison in Language Models
items.body: How does data shape language model (LM) behavior throughout pretraining? We investigate this question through a case study on entity comparison, e.g., Between France and Brazil, which country is larger?, across nine comparison tasks spanning five entity types. We begin with controlled experiments in which we train small LMs (163M parameters) on mixtures of natural text from pretraining corpora and synthetic task data. Our analysis identifies three distinct phases of learning: (1) an early phase where the LM selects entities by frequency, (2) a middle phase where the LM selects entities by position in the prompt (first vs. last mentioned entity), and (3) a late phase where the LM selects the entity that is the correct answer. We show that the emergence of these three phases is causally determined by statistical properties of the training data. With small amounts of task-specific synthetic data, we observe only the first two phases and the model fails to learn the task; with large amounts, the model jumps directly from the frequency-based heuristic to solving the task correctly. Moreover, changing the entity frequency distribution from a naturally occurring Zipfian distribution (a small number of entities are very common and the vast majority are rare) to a uniform one weakens the frequency phase and speeds up learning of the task. Lastly, we show that the three phases of training dynamics from our controlled experiments appear in the open source model OLMo-2 32B. Together, our findings demonstrate that properties of pretraining data are causal drivers of heuristic learning and show that small-scale synthetic experiments can predict training dynamics at larger scales.
items.title_ko: 사전 훈련 데이터 통계가 언어 모델의 개체 비교 학습 단계에 미치는 영향 연구

items.title: Protein Language Models Fail To Capture Contact Predictions Under Invariant Relabeling
items.body: Protein language models (pLMs) produce highly accurate contact maps from single-sequence inputs. People often take this accuracy as proof that these models implicitly learn invariant coevolutionary statistics, extracting the same signals as classical alignment-based methods like Potts. In this work, we introduce a diagnostic framework around a global bijective relabeling of the amino-acid alphabet. This transformation permutes residue letters while leaving all alignment-level information, column entropies, and pairwise edit distances unchanged. Pseudolikelihood Potts models and inverse-covariance estimators remain invariant under this transformation, but pLMs fail the test. Across multiple architectures (ESM-2, MSA Transformer, AMPLIFY) and model scales (8M to 3B parameters), pLM contact maps collapse under arbitrary relabeling. Using Hamming distance controls and biochemical grouping interventions, we attempt to isolate what likely causes this degradation and find that these models rely on explicit, canonical residue identities (``alphabet anchoring'') rather than pure coevolutionary statistics. Increasing scale makes models more responsive to biochemical classes, but their performance still degrades under relabeling. Our findings show a gap between how pLMs and classical coevolutionary models compute contacts. More broadly, our work shows how diagnostic perturbations that leave classical models provably unchanged can expose hidden representation biases and prevent over-reliance on neural black boxes in biological modeling.

items.title: Context Graph: Explainable Multi-Agent Decision Chains in AI-RAN
items.body: AI-RAN distributes network control across multiple autonomous agents, namely xApps and rApps operating over shared radio resources. When an alert or degradation appears, operators currently lack a structured way to trace which decision caused it, what context triggered that decision, and how other agents interacted. Existing explainability tools focus on single-model feature attribution or linear event logging, neither of which captures cross-agent decision chains. We propose the Context Graph, a heterogeneous directed graph that organizes policies, measurements, decisions, and alerts into a queryable explanation layer. Its foundational primitive is the Decision-Event node acting as a causal junction, where incoming edges capture triggering context and outgoing edges track downstream consequences that are progressively upgraded through counterfactual verification. Instantiated over existing E2, A1, and O1 data flows, our proof-of-concept demonstrates that compliance and diagnosis queries are resolved at sub-millisecond latency over graphs of tens of thousands of nodes, while reliably distinguishing true causal impacts from spurious correlations.
items.title_ko: AI-RAN에서 다중 에이전트 의사결정 체인을 설명하는 'Context Graph' 제안
items.summary_ko: AI-RAN(AI-Radio Access Network) 환경에서 경고 또는 성능 저하 발생 시, 기존 설명 가능성 도구들은 단일 모델이나 선형 이벤트 로깅에 초점을 맞춰 에이전트 간의 복잡한 의사결정 체인을 포착하지 못했습니다. Context Graph는 이러한 문제를 해결하기 위해, 어떤 결정이 특정 상황을 유발했고 다른 에이전트와 어떻게 상호작용했는지를 추적하는 구조화된 방법을 제안합니다.

items.title: Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition: Information, Uncertainty, and Conditional Regime Inference
items.body: When do mode energies preserve regime information as measurement quality changes? Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition (sKMD) fits joint regime laws on signed KMD mode coordinates and transfers the reference mode posterior to regime probabilities and conditional reconstructions. For centered Gaussian regimes with independently varying known noise variances, fixed coordinate energies retain the full regime posterior precisely when all classes share their cross-covariances and class variances can differ only at isolated vertices of the covariance graph. We extend the characterization to nonzero means and show that freely varying correlated noise forces a fixed linear log-odds decoder to retain the full quadratic feature span even for two distinct centered regimes. At fixed quality, a three-regime example has no sufficient two-energy basis. Its smallest Bayes log-loss gap over bases of condition number at most $κ$ has sharp order $κ^{-1}$. Exact Bayes energy posteriors supply numerical gap estimates for specified bases. Additional bounds relate feature compression, independently learned mode spans and sensor-noise error to log loss. Two controlled experiments with 64 independent panels each show that signed information can improve prediction over energy summaries, while integration gives small gains over strong signed controls and depends on how the competing point rule is calibrated and how accurately observation noise is measured.
items.title_ko: 확률론적 커널 모드 분해(sKMD) 연구: 정보, 불확실성 및 조건부 체제 추론

items.title: datasette-leaflet 0.3
items.body:
Release: datasette-leaflet 0.3

OpenStreetMap have a very reasonable policy that hits to their hosted tile server should send a referrer header. Datasette table pages used the Referrer-Policy: no-referrer HTTP header, causing plugins that loaded tiles from OpenStreetMap to violate that policy.

datasette-leaflet is the plugin that loads a bundled Leaflet so other Datasette plugins can depend on it. It now sets the referrer policy on the tile requests themselves to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, passing the host but not the full path to the page.

Tags: leaflet, datasette, openstreetmap

items.body:

AI Twitter Recap

Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Google's Fast Gemini 4 Tier Ships Broadly

Launch: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a speed-first model positioned alongside Carbon and Argon. Google says it completes tasks 2.5x faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash and edges Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, 51 vs 50 at default thinking and 54 at the new xhigh level (DeepMind, Koray Kavukcuoglu).
Specs and pricing: The model offers four thinking levels (low, medium, high and xhigh) and a 1M context window. It costs $1.50/$7.50 per million input/output tokens, with a 95% discount on cached input (Phil Schmid, Artificial Analysis).

Official claims: Google reports 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and more than 3x Gemini 3.8 Flash on Terminal-Bench 4.1. It also claims more than 5x fewer fabricated claims, #1 on Vals Tax Agent Bench and leading results on AutomationBench-AA and Agents' Last Exam (Google).

Availability: Hydrogen is available on all Gemini API tiers, including a free tier in AI Studio. It is the default model in Search AI Mode, and free Gemini app users get it through auto-selection. Paid Pro and Ultra subscribers can use it in Antigravity (Sundar Pichai, GeminiApp, Search).

Orchestrator multi-model mode: In Antigravity, Carbon plans while Hydrogen writes and tests code. Google says this reaches near-Carbon success on Terminal-Bench 4.0 with 24% less quota and 19% faster completion. It is rolling out to Ultra subscribers (Google, Mohan).

Artificial Analysis measurements: The independent results show a mixed profile.
Intelligence and cost: At xhigh, Hydrogen scores 54, one point behind Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max). Its cost is about 32% of Sonnet's but about 2.5x Sol's. Cost per task is $3.16 at xhigh and $1.87 at high. Output speed is about 200 tok/s (AA).

Strengths: Hydrogen has an 8% hallucination rate on AA-Omniscience, versus 43% for Sonnet and 52% for Sol. It also shares the #1 score on GDP.pdf visual reasoning.

Weaknesses: It scores 54% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at both high and xhigh, below Sonnet at 64% and Sol at 56%.

Third-party leaderboards:
Agent Arena: Hydrogen debuts at #5 with +14.8% net improvement across 6.5k sessions. It is the fastest model in the top 10 at 5.3 minutes per task median, with a median cost of $1.6 per task (Arena).

Code Arena WebDev: It ranks #10 with 1703 points (Arena).

Vals Index: It is #6 at 68.5%, 2 points behind Carbon at 38% of Carbon's price (Vals).

Coding agents: CursorBench rises to 54.3% from 39.6% for 3.8 Flash (Cursor). Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 shows 38.2%, just behind Sol (Cognition). SWE-sweep shows 13.5%, versus 9.5% for Astra (KLieret).

Caveats from users:
Runaway reasoning: One tester saw xhigh spend 131K thinking tokens and about $1.08 without answering a jersey-number image question. The same tester reports budget exhaustion on 1.8% of a text benchmark (skalskip92).

Weak spots: Hydrogen scored 1% on MazeBench (patience_cave).

Pricing structure: Simon Willison says Hydrogen is only a 25% discount on the Carbon/Argon token price, though those models reportedly double in price on Dec 1 (simonw).

Speed: Theo disputes the "built for speed" framing based on his own timings (theo).

Open-Weight Releases: Inkling 2 Small Leads

Inkling 2 Small: Thinking Machines released the weights under Apache 2.0 (thinkymachines, Mira Murati).
Size: It is a 594B-total / 17B-active MoE with text and image input and up to 1M context (HF).

Architecture: New components include attention residuals with a q/k/v split, gated attention, a dynamic attention sink, dynamic shortconv and value norm (Songlin Yang). Experts use NVFP4 in layers 0–39 and MXFP8 in the last eight, with SWA widened to 1k and softcaps on the LM head and SwiGLU (eliebakouch).

Day-0 serving: On vLLM, it fits on one GB200/GB300 node and reaches up to 630 tok/s per user at TP4. Its native DSpark speculator has an acceptance length of about 3.5 at T=1.0 (vLLM, details). SGLang reports 576 tok/s per user at batch 1 on Vera Rubin and text-plus-vision RL on 8 Blackwells (SGLang). SkyRL validates MXFP8, BF16 and LoRA RL (erictang).

Evals: It is the #1 US open model on Code Arena WebDev at 1647 points (Arena). On Agent Arena it is #2 among open models, with a median cost of $0.26 per task (Arena). It also holds the top open-model spot on MathArena's BrokenArXiv (MathArena).

Edge0-145B/120B: These are device-native open-weight models. The developer claims 86.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, versus 78.2% for Claude Opus 4.6, in about 29GB of memory at 75+ tok/s decode (Samuel Zeng). These figures are vendor claims.

Perplexity Decider v1.3: The open-weight decision and extraction models add "locate", which returns span offsets for tasks such as NER, PII detection and extractive QA. Perplexity says the release is 6.54 points more accurate than its production classifiers on 63 tasks, and the models are free on OpenRouter for one week (Aravind Srinivas).

Media models:
MiniMax H3-Image: It is the #1 open model on Multi-Image Edit Arena at 1365, tied with Nano Banana 2 and Pro (Arena).

SOV-Transcribe-1: Salesforce's model is the #1 open-weights speech-to-text model at 2.3% AA-WER, with 4.6B active parameters (AA).

Checkpoint Forensics, Chinese Compute and Export Controls

GPU fingerprinting claim: Will Depue says initialization patterns in released weights identify the GPU type that produced them (report).
Findings: He reports six Chinese models, including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3 and MiniMax-M3, were initialized on Blackwell systems, four of them on Grace Blackwell. He says a B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash's starting weights bit for bit, and a GB200 reproduced Kimi K3's at a correlation of 0.999995.

Validation: He reports a 24-for-24 match on models with publicly disclosed hardware and match strengths of 49–1,385 sigma. He says Kimi K3's weights were created by at least 64 processes, all on Grace Blackwell (rebuttal).

Scale estimate: He estimates 2–3K Blackwells each for the largest runs. He says senior OpenAI and Anthropic researchers verified the work but are not on record (request for verifiers).

Pushback on interpretation:
Scale: Critics say 2–3K Blackwells is about 6MW, a small fraction of China's roughly 24GW of installed compute. On that view, the result could indicate export controls are working rather than failing (teortaxesTex, scale note).

Ascend training: Others note that Depue's analysis also places DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and LongCat on Ascend chips (zephyr).

Novelty: Some researchers say Blackwell use by Chinese labs was already widely known (eliebakouch).

Proposed Commerce rule: The reported rule would restrict Chinese access to overseas AI data centers

Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Google의 빠른 Gemini 4 티어 광범위하게 출시

출시: Google DeepMind는 속도 우선 모델인 Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 Carbon 및 Argon과 함께 출시했습니다. Google은 이 모델이 Gemini 3.8 Flash보다 2.5배 빠르게 작업을 완료하고, 기본 사고(default thinking)에서 인공 분석 지능 지수(Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index)에서 Argon보다 51 대 50으로 앞서며, 새로운 xhigh 수준에서는 54점을 기록했다고 말합니다 (DeepMind, Koray Kavukcuoglu).
사양 및 가격: 이 모델은 4가지 사고 수준(low, medium, high 및 xhigh)과 1M 컨텍스트 창을 제공합니다. 백만 입력/출력 토큰당 $1.50/$7.50의 비용이 들며, 캐시된 입력에는 95% 할인이 적용됩니다 (Phil Schmid, Artificial Analysis).

공식 주장: Google은 Terminal-Bench 4.0에서 57%, Terminal-Bench 4.1에서 Gemini 3.8 Flash보다 3배 이상 높은 성능을 보고합니다. 또한 조작된 주장이 5배 이상 적고, Vals Tax Agent Bench에서 1위, AutomationBench-AA 및 Agents' Last Exam에서 선두 결과를 기록했다고 주장합니다 (Google).

가용성: Hydrogen은 AI Studio의 무료 티어를 포함하여 모든 Gemini API 티어에서 사용할 수 있습니다. Search AI Mode의 기본 모델이며, 무료 Gemini 앱 사용자는 자동 선택을 통해 이를 이용할 수 있습니다. 유료 Pro 및 Ultra 구독자는 Antigravity에서 사용할 수 있습니다 (Sundar Pichai, GeminiApp, Search).

Orchestrator 멀티 모델 모드: Antigravity에서 Carbon은 계획을 세우고 Hydrogen은 코드를 작성하고 테스트합니다. Google은 이 방식이 Carbon에 가까운 Terminal-Bench 4.0 성공률을 24% 적은 할당량과 19% 빠른 완료 시간으로 달성한다고 말합니다. 이는 Ultra 구독자에게 rollout되고 있습니다 (Google, Mohan).

인공 분석 측정: 독립적인 결과는 혼합된 프로필을 보여줍니다.
지능 및 비용: xhigh에서 Hydrogen은 54점을 기록하여 Claude Sonnet 5.5 (최대) 및 GPT-6.1 Sol (최대)보다 1점 뒤쳐집니다. 비용은 Sonnet의 약 32%이지만 Sol의 약 2.5배입니다. 작업당 비용은 xhigh에서 $3.16, high에서 $1.87입니다. 출력 속도는 약 200 tok/s입니다 (AA).

강점: Hydrogen은 AA-Omniscience에서 8%의 환각률을 보였으며, Sonnet은 43%, Sol은 52%였습니다. 또한 GDP.pdf 시각적 추론에서 1위 점수를 공유합니다.

약점: Terminal-Bench 4.0에서 high 및 xhigh 모두에서 54%를 기록하여 Sonnet의 64% 및 Sol의 56%보다 낮습니다.

타사 리더보드:
Agent Arena: Hydrogen은 6.5k 세션에 걸쳐 +14.8%의 순 개선율로 5위에 데뷔했습니다. 상위 10개 모델 중 가장 빠른 모델로, 작업당 중간 시간은 5.3분, 작업당 중간 비용은 $1.6입니다 (Arena).

Code Arena WebDev: 1703점으로 10위를 기록했습니다 (Arena).

Vals Index: 68.5%로 6위이며, Carbon보다 2점 뒤쳐지지만 Carbon 가격의 38% 수준입니다 (Vals).

코딩 에이전트: CursorBench는 3.8 Flash의 39.6%에서 54.3%로 상승했습니다 (Cursor). Cognition의 FrontierCode 2.0은 38.2%를 보여 Sol 바로 뒤에 있습니다 (Cognition). SWE-sweep은 13.5%를 보여 Astra의 9.5%보다 높습니다 (KLieret).

사용자 주의사항:
폭주 추론: 한 테스터는 xhigh가 저지 번호 이미지 질문에 답변하지 않고 131K의 사고 토큰과 약 $1.08를 사용했다고 보고했습니다. 동일한 테스터는 텍스트 벤치마크의 1.8%에서 예산 소진을 보고합니다 (skalskip92).

약점: Hydrogen은 MazeBench에서 1%를 기록했습니다 (patience_cave).

가격 구조: Simon Willison은 Hydrogen이 Carbon/Argon 토큰 가격의 25% 할인에 불과하다고 말했지만, 해당 모델들은 12월 1일에 가격이 두 배로 오른다고 합니다 (simonw).

속도: Theo는 자신의 측정치를 기반으로

items.title: AI Ambition: ArtCraft Cloned Photoshop and Now Wants to "Rebuild Everything"
items.body:
The theme of day two of the AI Engineer Code Summit in San Francisco was increasing ambition using AI. And there have been few projects as ambitious as ArtCraft in the AI era. So far the fledgling company has released 17 open source versions of popular software tools, starting with a Photoshop alternative built from scratch in Rust called PhotoCraft.

You could feel the excitement in the room this morning when ArtCraft founder and CEO Brandon Thomas presented a kind of manifesto for AI-based open source at AIE Code. When he mentioned that ArtCraft had cloned Adobe’s Acrobat, with a product called PdfCraft, it got a round of applause from the audience. In wrapping up, his rallying cries of “let's take back the entire internet” and “let's rebuild everything” were greeted with whoops and cheers.

Thomas began his presentation by reliving the internet’s early history. In his view, the web started out with the right intentions, but things got screwed up once Web 2.0 hit the mainstream.

“We had a bunch of chat applications that were completely open,” he said, regarding the 1990s internet. “So, IRC is like Discord, but you can spin up your own servers that you actually own. You can use whatever programs to automate them and interrogate them without rules.”

His point wasn’t necessarily that everything was open source, but that web users could freely build things. With Flash, for example — a commercial animation tool eventually acquired by Adobe — “kids were making all kinds of animations.”

When Web 2.0 came along, with its superior broadband and smartphones, “it brought everybody into the fold.” Thomas acknowledged that this widened the scope of internet software, but at the cost of that freedom to build with leading apps.

“The diffuse, experimental, early web started to disappear,” he said. “The APIs got taken away from us, and then we started seeing distribution being gatekept by the big providers.”

It seems Adobe in particular annoyed Thomas. He described getting billed with an unexpected fee when he cancelled a monthly plan.

“It's really frustrating that the web — that was once really, really promising and open and free — has turned into this extractive, owned, rent-seeking world.”

This inspired him to start ArtCraft, “with the ethos of ‘let's build everything open source.’” A message even anti-AI people have gotten behind, according to Thomas.

In addition to PhotoCraft, they’ve copied other apps in the Adobe suite, cloned Figma, and created a Microsoft-like word processor called WordCraft. There are also independent apps such as SolidCraft, a community-led CAD project distributed through ArtCraft’s launcher.

Thomas reiterated that these AI-built applications are 100% open — “not only the desktop apps, but the actual infrastructure as well.”

PhotoCraft: The development process

ArtCraft is starting with rewriting familiar tools. Thomas’s longer-term vision is for users (such as artists who were previously using Photoshop) to tailor the software to their own workflows.

As he framed it, they want to “undo what had happened during Web 2.0, when everything became owned and consolidated and gatekept, and just give people back their applications.”

AI is the means to achieve that, he said.

But aren’t there already open source alternatives to Photoshop, like GIMP?

“GIMP isn't really used by artists,” said Thomas during his presentation. “We actually observed artists vibe coding their own workflows on top of the software that we gave them.”

To begin creating PhotoCraft, the team gave an AI model a detailed prompt outlining Photoshop’s tools, data structures and file importers. After that, they “laid out a large, large prompt to say, let's build out the application.”

As part of that process, they made everything MCP and CLI compatible.

Within 24 hours, said Thomas, “we were looking at a pretty good approximation of what Photoshop was — and it kind of blew our minds away.”

PhotoCraft interface; via ArtCraft website

Thomas noted that PhotoCraft is “still not at 100% parity” — he said they’ve just passed 60% — but the team has set an internal goal to reach as close to 100% as possible. (The project’s GitHub claims about 76% parity for feature breadth and about 46% for professional readiness.)

“Right now, we want to fill the muscle memory of all the artists that use Adobe. So we are going for Adobe, their interface and ‘look and feel’ directly.”

But after ArtCraft has achieved that, they plan to “build new apps that have new interfaces that are more agentic.”

A big reaction

Thomas said he was surprised by the amount of attention PhotoCraft, in particular, has gotten — ranging from the New York Times requesting an interview, to a swelling of its open source community to about 4,000 developers.

“I'm still struggling to bear with what has happened. It struck a nerve with people. They felt sort of maligned by Adobe and other tech companies. And what we built has really resonated with them.”

After his presentation, Thomas was mobbed by AIE Code attendees.

ArtCraft’s apps are being downloaded at the rate of about 1.7 million per day, which Thomas said is still accelerating.

In addition to the 17 official apps, there are around 300 being developed by the community, he added.

Rust is key, but there have been technical challenges

Other than the AI technology, Thomas said that Rust was a crucial part of making the apps performant — he claimed that PhotoCraft opens ten times faster than Photoshop, for example.

“Rust was probably essential in this product's success,” he said. “We've seen people do it in Electron before, but for high-quality creative apps, you really need something that's native.”

For those engineers who are not experts in Rust, Thomas has good news for you.

“Do you need to know Rust to start using Rust today as an engineer? Definitely not. [...] Your agents will drive it just fine.”

However, Thomas admitted that not everything has gone swimmingly.

“We've run into a lot of gotchas — like permissions, GitHub, scaling, CI,” he said. “CI is falling over. We've been spinning up our own. We found a good place to get RAM on co-located servers.”

But they have found an equilibrium on what agents can do and what needs to be handled by people.

“If you're doing backend work or things that require schema migrations [or] API design, let your humans do that. But for desktop apps and games and anything that's basically immutable, throw your agents at it and give them full confidence.”

And it turns out, there’s even an ArtCraft solution for you there.

“AutoCraft is a completely autonomous software factory that we're going to open source.”

AI open source FTW

There’s no doubting the ambition of Brandon Thomas and his ArtCraft company.

“We can open source the entire world,” he proclaimed at the end of his presentation. “Let's own our apps, our infra, our protocols, our models — all of it.”

It’s a big vision, potentially even on the scale of Linux if its current downloads growth rate continues. But, ironically perhaps, what intrigues me most about ArtCraft is the growth of its human contributor community. After all, that’s what the original web got most right: human collaboration at scale.

The big difference from the 1990s is that now it’s agents doing the bulk of the development work.
items.body_ko:
샌프란시스코에서 열린 AI Engineer Code Summit 둘째 날의 주제는 AI를 활용한 야망 증대였습니다. 그리고 AI 시대에 ArtCraft만큼 야심 찬 프로젝트는 거의 없었습니다. 지금까지 이 신생 회사는 인기 있는 소프트웨어 도구 17가지의 오픈 소스 버전을 출시했으며, Rust로 처음부터 다시 만든 Photoshop 대안인 PhotoCraft부터 시작했습니다.

오늘 아침 ArtCraft의 설립자이자 CEO인 Brandon Thomas가 AIE Code에서 AI 기반 오픈 소스에 대한 일종의 선언문을 발표했을 때, 회의실에 흥분이 가득했습니다. 그가 ArtCraft가 Adobe의 Acrobat을 PdfCraft라는 제품으로 복제했다고 언급했을 때, 청중으로부터 박수갈채를 받았습니다. 마무리하며 “인터넷 전체를 되찾자”와 “모든 것을 다시 만들자”는 그의 외침은 환호와 갈채로 이어졌습니다.

Thomas는 인터넷의 초기 역사를 되새기면서 발표를 시작했습니다. 그의 견해로는 웹은 올바른 의도로 시작했지만, Web 2.0이 주류가 되면서 상황이 엉망이 되었습니다.

1990년대 인터넷에 대해 그는 “완전히 개방된 수많은 채팅 애플리케이션이 있었습니다”라고 말했습니다. “그래서 IRC는 Discord와 같지만, 사용자가 실제로 소유하는 서버를 직접 구축할 수 있습니다. 규칙 없이 원하는 프로그램을 사용하여 자동화하고 쿼리할 수 있습니다.”

그의 요점은 모든 것이 오픈 소스였다는 것이 아니라, 웹 사용자들이 자유롭게 무언가를 만들 수 있었다는 것입니다. 예를 들어, 궁극적으로 Adobe에 인수된 상업용 애니메이션 도구인 Flash를 통해 “아이들이 온갖 애니메이션을 만들었습니다.”

Web 2.0이 더 우수한 광대역과 스마트폰과 함께 등장하면서, “모든 사람을 참여시켰습니다.” Thomas는 이것이 인터넷 소프트웨어의 범위를 넓혔지만, 선도적인 앱으로 자유롭게 구축할 수 있는 자유를 희생했다고 인정했습니다.

그는 “분산되고 실험적인 초기 웹은 사라지기 시작했습니다”라고 말했습니다. “API는 우리에게서 빼앗겼고, 그 다음에는 대형 공급업체들에 의해 배포가 통제되는 것을 보기 시작했습니다.”

특히 Adobe가 Thomas를 짜증 나게 한 것 같습니다. 그는 월간 요금제를 취소했을 때 예상치 못한 요금이 청구되었다고 설명했습니다.

“한때 정말 유망하고 개방적이며 자유로웠던 웹이 이처럼 착취적이고 소유되며 임대료를 추구하는 세상으로 변했다는 것이 정말 답답합니다.”

이것이 그가 “모든 것을 오픈 소스로 만들자”는 정신으로 ArtCraft를 시작하게 된 계기가 되었습니다. Thomas에 따르면, 심지어 반(反) AI 사람들도 이 메시지를 지지했습니다.

PhotoCraft 외에도 그들은 Adobe 제품군의 다른 앱들을 복사하고, Figma를 복제했으며, WordCraft라는 Microsoft와 유사한 워드 프로세서를 만들었습니다. ArtCraft의 런처를 통해 배포되는 커뮤니티 주도 CAD 프로젝트인 SolidCraft와 같은 독립적인 앱들도 있습니다.

Thomas는 이러한 AI 기반 애플리케이션이 100% 개방되어 있으며, “데스크톱 앱뿐만 아니라 실제 인프라도 마찬가지”라고 다시 강조했습니다.

PhotoCraft: 개발 프로세스

ArtCraft는 익숙한 도구를 다시 작성하는 것부터 시작합니다. Thomas의 장기적인 비전은 사용자(예: 이전에 Photoshop을 사용했던 아티스트)가 자신의 워크플로우에 맞게 소프트웨어를 조정하는 것입니다.

그가 설명했듯이, 그들은 “Web 2.0 동안 모든 것이 소유되고 통합되며 통제되었던 것을 되돌리고, 사람들에게 다시 그들의 애플리케이션을 돌려주기를” 원합니다.

AI가 그것을 달성하기 위한 수단이라고 그는 말했습니다.

하지만 GIMP와 같은 Photoshop의 오픈 소스 대안이 이미 있지 않나요?

Thomas는 발표 중에 “GIMP는 아티스트들이 실제로 사용하지 않습니다”라고 말했습니다. “우리는 아티스트들이 우리가 제공한 소프트웨어 위에 자신만의 워크플로우를 코딩하는 것을 실제로 관찰했습니다.”

PhotoCraft를 만들기 시작하기 위해 팀은 AI 모델에 Photoshop의 도구, 데이터 구조 및 파일 가져오기 기능을 자세히 설명하는 프롬프트를 제공했습니다. 그 후, 그들은 “애플리케이션을 구축하자고 말하는 크고 큰 프롬프트를 만들었습니다.”

그 과정의 일부로, 그들은 모든 것을 MCP 및 CLI 호환으로 만들었습니다.

Thomas는 24시간 이내에 “Photoshop이 무엇인지에 대한 꽤 좋은 근사치를 보고 있었고, 그것은 우리를 정말 놀라게 했습니다”라고 말했습니다.

PhotoCraft 인터페이스; ArtCraft 웹사이트 경유

Thomas는 PhotoCraft가 “아직 100% 동등한 수준은 아니다”라고 언급했습니다. 그는 60%를 조금 넘었다고 말했지만, 팀은 가능한 한 100%에 가깝게 도달하기 위한 내부 목표를 설정했습니다. (이 프로젝트의 GitHub는 기능 범위에서 약 76%, 전문가 준비도에서 약 46%의 동등성을 주장합니다.)

“지금 당장은 Adobe를 사용하는 모든 아티스트의 근육 기억을 채우고 싶습니다. 그래서 우리는 Adobe의 인터페이스와 ‘룩앤필’을 직접적으로 따르고 있습니다.”

하지만 ArtCraft가 그것을 달성한 후에는 “더 에이전트적인 새로운 인터페이스를 가진 새로운 앱들을 만들 계획”입니다.

큰 반응

Thomas는 특히 PhotoCraft가 받은 관심의 양에 놀랐다고 말했습니다. 뉴욕 타임즈의 인터뷰 요청부터 오픈 소스 커뮤니티가 약 4,000명의 개발자로 불어나는 등 다양했습니다.

“무슨 일이 일어났는지 아직도 감당하기 힘듭니다. 사람들의 신경을 건드렸습니다. 그들은 Adobe와 다른 기술 회사들에 의해 일종의 피해를 입었다고 느꼈습니다. 그리고 우리가 만든 것이 그들에게 정말 공감을 얻었습니다.”

발표 후 Thomas는 AIE Code 참석자들에게 둘러싸였습니다.

ArtCraft 앱은 하루에 약 170만 건의 속도로 다운로드되고 있으며, Thomas는 이 속도가 계속 가속화되고 있다고 말했습니다.

17개의 공식 앱 외에도 커뮤니티에서 약 300개가 개발 중이라고 그는 덧붙였습니다.

AI 기술 외에 Thomas는 Rust가 앱의 성능을 높이는 데 중요한 부분이었다고 말했습니다. 예를 들어 PhotoCraft가 Photoshop보다 10배 더 빠르게 열린다고 주장했습니다.
